In [[geometry]], the '''parabiaugmented hexagonal prism''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|55}}}}). As the name suggests, it can be constructed by doubly augmenting a hexagonal [[prism (geometry)|prism]] by attaching [[square pyramid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|1}}}}) to two of its nonadjacent, parallel (opposite) equatorial faces. Attaching the pyramids to nonadjacent, nonparallel equatorial faces yields a [[metabiaugmented hexagonal prism]] ({{math|''J''{{sub|56}}}}). (The solid obtained by attaching pyramids to adjacent equatorial faces is not convex, and thus not a Johnson solid.)
